newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish court charges 49 for U.S. embassy protest.
newsitem.headline: Turkish court charges 49 for U.S. embassy protest.

text.p: A Turkish security court on Thursday charged 49 people for protesting outside the U.S. embassy against a Turkish army cross-border operation in northern Iraq, human rights activists said.
"Forty-nine people were charged by the Ankara court without any legal reason," the Human Rights Association said in a statement.

The suspects were among more than 200 people who assembled at the U.S. embassy in central Ankara last Saturday to lay a wreath in protest against Turkey's operation against Kurdish rebels in northern Iraq.
The state-run Anatolian news agency said the 49, members of leftist parties and human rights groups, had been arrested for "assisting an outlawed organisation".
The charge, usually levelled at suspected Kurdish rebel sympathisers, carries a penalty of between three and five years in prison.
NATO ally Washington strongly backs Turkey against the Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) guerrillas and is a major arms supplier to Ankara.
Turkish troops, backed by air support, have been in northern Iraq since May 14 when they launched an operation to attack PKK positions in the mountainous region.
Arab countries have condemned the military push as a threat to Iraq's sovereignty.
